title: Underlying derived invariants comparison for finite-dimensional profinite representations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. Let $G$ be any profinite group. Put $A=\underline E$, $C(P)=\{f\in C(P,\Omega): f(P)\text{ lies in one finite subextension}\}$, $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$, and $c:C\hookrightarrow B$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Use the action categories $\mathcal A_G(R)$ of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], their ordinary unbounded derived categories and the ordinary total right derived invariant-submodule functors $R\Gamma_G$ [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. For $R=C,B$, let
$$F_R(K)=\operatorname{ev}_*R\Gamma_G(R\otimes_A^L K),\qquad K\in D(\mathcal A_G(A)),$$
where $G$ acts trivially on $R$, diagonally on the tensor, and $\operatorname{ev}_*$ evaluates a condensed module at the one-point profinite set and forgets scalars. These are exact functors to $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. Scalar inclusion induces a natural transformation $\alpha:F_C\to F_B$ compatible with the exact functors' shift isomorphisms; it is induced on a K-flat model by $z\otimes v\mapsto c(z)\otimes v$ and on derived invariants by scalar restriction and the inclusion of invariant submodules.

For every finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $W$ with continuous $E$-linear $G$-action, put $\underline W(P)=C(P,W)$. Then the actual morphism
$$\alpha_{\underline W[0]}:\operatorname{ev}_*R\Gamma_G(C\otimes_A^L\underline W)\longrightarrow\operatorname{ev}_*R\Gamma_G(B\otimes_A^L\underline W)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. No internal condensed isomorphism is asserted before evaluation, and no finite cohomological dimension or finite generation of $G$ is required. In particular the claim does not identify these derived invariants with underived continuous cochain complexes for the incomplete norm field $\Omega$.

proof.text: Choose an $E$-basis of $W$, of size $d\geq0$. Its coordinate maps and their inverse are continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous], since $E$ is a complete nontrivially normed field and $W$ has its finite-dimensional norm topology. Hence $\underline W\cong A^d$. A finite free module in degree zero is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex]: tensoring an acyclic complex with $A^d$ is a finite direct sum of that complex and is acyclic. Consequently $R\otimes_A^L\underline W$ is represented by the actual action module $N_R=R^d$ in degree zero, for $R=C,B$. Its action is the matrix $\rho(g)\in\mathrm{GL}_d(E)$ extended to $R$; its coefficient map is entrywise $c$. These basis choices are used only to prove invertibility of the specified morphism. For $d=0$ both sides and the comparison are zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), arithmetic coefficient-topology input; agent proof, not a proof present in the blueprint.

proof.text: For every profinite $P$, put $A[P]$ for the free internal $A$-module on $P$. The actual scalar extensions $R\otimes_A^L A[P]$ are $R[P]$: the sheafification of $S\mapsto\bigoplus_{S\to P}A(S)$ has maps to $M$ in bijection with $M(P)$, by sending the generator of $f:S\to P$ to $f^*m$. It is therefore both $A[P]$ and $j_{P!}A_P$. Hence $A[P]$ is flat by [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat], and the ordinary scalar-extension identification follows by the free-module adjunction. Apply [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] to identify the derived internal-function columns over $R$ with those over $A$ after restriction. For $B$ and for each finite $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, [lem-sfb-normed-scalar-profinite-hom-acyclic], applied also with its finite intermediate field equal to $F$, identifies the corresponding column for a rank-$d$ module with continuous $V_F$-valued functions on $P$, in degree zero. These are finite direct sums of the scalar calculation. The comparison is the canonical map from ordinary to derived Hom, not an arbitrary object isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), arithmetic coefficient-topology input; agent proof, not a proof present in the blueprint.

proof.text: The finite extensions containing $E$ are cofinal among all finite subextensions: take the compositum with $E$, as in [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions]. By [lem-sfb-qlbar-point-abelian-colimit] the actual finite-subextension-valued $C$ is their colimit; the same holds as $A$-modules, since its sectionwise module operations commute with the coprojections. Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-derived-functions-filtered-colimit] to the restricted $A$-module diagram $(\underline F)^d$. In conjunction with step 2 it identifies the $C$ column with $\operatorname{colim}_{F\supseteq E} C(-\times P,V_F)[0]$. Its sections are exactly continuous functions whose coordinates all lie in one finite $F$: filtered sectionwise colimits on the coherent profinite site satisfy sheaf descent, since any covering refines a finite one and the matching condition uses finite fibre products. A finite family of coordinates has a common $F$ by compositum. The comparison from this column to the $B$ column is the literal inclusion into all continuous $V_\Omega$-valued functions. Both column identifications are normalized by evaluation and natural in $P$ and in coefficient maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), arithmetic coefficient-topology input; agent proof, not a proof present in the blueprint.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] to $N_C,N_B$ and set $P=G^n$ in the preceding steps. The ordinary-to-derived column maps form a cosimplicial comparison: interior and last faces are parameter precomposition, and the first is pullback followed by the action matrix $\rho(g_1)$ over $E$. Evaluation normalization makes these squares commute; the latter equality is $c(\rho(g_1)v)=\rho(g_1)c(v)$, also for continuously varying $g_1$. Resolve the two bar diagrams compatibly in nonnegative vertical degrees. Their column maps are quasi-isomorphisms by steps 2–3, so [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] identifies their total complexes. Only finite diagonals occur. Evaluation at the one-point profinite set is exact by [lem-zl-contractible-derived-sections-tensor], with $T=*$, and commutes with these finite sums. Thus the actual $\alpha_{\underline W[0]}$ is represented, after forgetting scalars, by the cochain inclusion
$$i:C^\bullet_{\mathrm{fin}}(G,V_\Omega)\hookrightarrow C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_\Omega).$$
Here $C^n_{\mathrm{fin}}$ consists of continuous functions $G^n\to V_\Omega$ with image in some $V_F$, with one $F$ for the whole function; $C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}$ has no such restriction. Both differentials are exactly the formula in [lem-sfb-local-norm-algcl-cocycle-descent]. Scalar naturality and the degree-zero invariant augmentation in the bar lemma ensure that this represents the stipulated inclusion-induced derived morphism.

proof.text: The degree-zero terms of both complexes are the same $V_\Omega$: any one vector has finitely many coordinates, all in a finite field. Their differentials agree, and the degree-one inclusion is injective. Their kernels in degree zero therefore coincide, so $H^0(i)$ is the identity on $V_\Omega^G$. All negative cohomology groups vanish because the complexes are nonnegative.

source.place: Paragraph (3), arithmetic coefficient-topology input; agent proof, not a proof present in the blueprint.

proof.text: Let $n\geq1$ and let $z\in C^n_{\mathrm{fin}}(G,V_\Omega)$ be a cocycle which is $db$ for a continuous $V_\Omega$-valued $(n-1)$-cochain. Choose $F\supseteq E$ with $z(G^n)\subseteq V_F$. By [lem-sfb-finite-subfield-continuous-linear-retraction] choose a continuous $E$-linear $p_F:\Omega\to F$ restricting to the identity on $F$. Apply it coordinatewise to obtain $p:V_\Omega\to V_F$. Every $\rho(g)$ has entries in $E$, so $p(\rho(g)v)=\rho(g)p(v)$. Consequently $p$ commutes with every summand of the displayed differential, and $d(pb)=p(db)=pz=z$. The cochain $pb$ is continuous and takes all its values in this one $V_F$. Hence $z$ is already a boundary in $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{fin}}$, proving injectivity of $H^n(i)$. For $n=1$, $b$ is a single vector and the same argument applies.

source.place: Paragraph (3), arithmetic coefficient-topology input; agent proof, not a proof present in the blueprint.

proof.text:
Let $n\geq1$ and let $z\in C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_\Omega)$ be a cocycle. Apply [lem-sfb-local-norm-algcl-cocycle-descent] to obtain an open $H$, a finite $F\supseteq E$, and $u\in Z^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V_F)$ with $[u]=\mathrm{res}[z]$ after inclusion. Put $m=[G:H]$, a positive finite integer. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-cochain-finite-index-transfer] simultaneously to $V_F\hookrightarrow V_\Omega$, using the same coset representatives. The continuous cochain $\mathrm{cor}(u)$ takes values in $V_F$; its class therefore comes from $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{fin}}(G,V_\Omega)$. Naturality and the stated homotopy give
$$i_*[\mathrm{cor}(u)]=\mathrm{cor}\,\mathrm{res}[z]=m[z].$$
Since $E$ has characteristic zero, $m^{-1}\in E\subseteq F$. The finite-field cocycle $m^{-1}\mathrm{cor}(u)$ maps to $[z]$. This proves surjectivity of $H^n(i)$ without any bound on $n$ or any restriction on $G$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), arithmetic coefficient-topology input; agent proof, not a proof present in the blueprint.

proof.text: Steps 5–7 show that the actual cochain map $i$ induces an isomorphism in every degree. By the definition of quasi-isomorphism and of the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its image is invertible in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. Step 4 identifies that image with $\alpha_{\underline W[0]}$, which proves the statement for this specified morphism. The use of the bar and acyclicity inputs is part of the proof, rather than an assumed identification with topological cohomology. No assertion is made for the internal condensed comparison prior to evaluation.

mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NN-254ff753e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First delivery of the item: no prior run and no repair note, so the 2026-10-21 re-split rules do not apply. Item statement unchanged, route is direct-images proof paragraph (3), no SGA. I read the item and all 4 new nodes in full.

Steps 1-4 reduce alpha_W to the cochain inclusion C_fin(G,V_Omega) -> C_cts(G,V_Omega). Inputs, each checked against its cited statement: finite-dimensional continuity gives W = A^d, which is K-flat; A[P] = j_P!A_P is flat; the scalar adjunction (no flatness hypothesis); normed-scalar acyclicity for Omega and, renaming its finite field, for each F; the qlbar colimit with compositum cofinality; the new filtered-colimit node; the bar lemma with scalar-restriction naturality; the first-quadrant comparison; exact evaluation at T=*.

Steps 5-8 are correct. In step 6, p = p_F^d commutes with E-matrices and hence with d. In step 7, cor(u) is V_F-valued by naturality, cor res = m up to homotopy, and m^-1 lies in E.

New nodes:
- local-norm-algcl-cocycle-descent is true, checked myself: Omega is a countable union of closed F_k, Baire on G^n gives a box of cosets of a normal open H, and the coboundary shift z' = z - d(z(.,b)) plus the cocycle identity at (a,.,.) makes z' F-valued on H^n. A bilinear counterexample attempt on prod Z_ell fails because its values would leave Omega. Not a restatement: weaker than surjectivity, and the transfer step is genuine.
- The transfer node is standard Shapiro/coinduction; open H makes coset maps locally constant.
- The retraction node follows from Ingleton Hahn-Banach (E is spherically complete).
- The filtered-colimit node is true via Stacks 0GN3 (sites-cohomology l.2630) on S x P slices.

Duplicate search (corestriction, Hahn-Banach, Baire, continuous cochain, filtered colimit, and the 10-22 sfb neighbours) found no duplicates; lem-sfb-dc-hom-filtered-colimit assumes this continuity rather than proving it.
